entities.name: Byzantine Empire under the Leonid dynasty
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Byzantine Empire under the Leonid dynasty (457-518 CE) governed one of the most turbulent transition periods in Byzantine history — the decades when the Eastern Roman Empire survived the fall of its Western counterpart, navigated the Monophysite theological controversy that threatened to split the Christian world, and attempted to reconquer Africa from the Vandals. The dynasty's founder Leo I (r. 457-474 CE) was the first emperor effectively chosen by the powerful Alan general Aspar — a barbarian in Roman service — before Leo outmaneuvered and had Aspar killed (471), demonstrating the emperor's ongoing struggle to control the military.

The dynasty is most noted for the disastrous Basiliscus Expedition (468 CE) — the largest naval expedition in ancient history at that point, involving 1,113 ships and 100,000 soldiers, sent to reconquer North Africa from the Vandals. The fleet was destroyed by Vandal fire-ships in a single night; the estimated loss (130,000 silver pounds) nearly bankrupted the Eastern Empire. This failure allowed the Vandals to continue for another 65 years until Justinian's 533 reconquest.

Emperor Zeno (r. 474-475, 476-491 CE) — an Isaurian of controversial origin — presided over the Western empire's formal end (476 CE) and resolved the succession crisis by inviting Theodoric the Ostrogoth to rule Italy (493 CE) 'on behalf of the Emperor' — technically preserving Roman sovereignty over Italy while removing the Ostrogoths from the Balkans. The dynasty ended when Anastasius I was chosen by empress Ariadne after Zeno's death — his 27-year reign built up an enormous treasury surplus that funded Justinian's ambitions.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Leonid dynasty — surviving while the Western Empire fell (476 CE), launching history's largest failed naval expedition (468 CE), and building the treasury surplus that enabled the Justinianic age — governed the critical transition period that ensured the Eastern Empire's survival while the West collapsed.
